newsitem.title: USA: Congressional leaders reach disaster aid accord.
newsitem.headline: Congressional leaders reach disaster aid accord.

text.p: Congressional leaders on Thursday announced agreement on a compromise bill to fund disaster aid and predicted it would pass free of political riders unacceptable to the White House.

Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott and Senate Minority Leader Tom Daschle announced the agreement on the Senate floor. A few minutes later House Majority Leader Dick Armey told reporters House Republicans also accepted the plan and predicted it would pass later in the day.

President Bill Clinton vetoed the bill Monday and urged Congress to approve it without provisions added by Republicans to avert another government shutdown and bar the use of sampling rather than person-by-person counts in the 2000 census.

The spending bill provides $5.6 billion for North and South Dakota and Minnesota, the states hit hardest by spring floods and 32 other states that suffered from winter storms, tornados and other natural disasters. It also provides $1.9 billion to pay for U.S. military operations in Bosnia and the Gulf. The remainder will pay for non-emergency programs.

As part of the compromise, Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott, Republican of Mississippi, won the right to bring up at a later date legislation to continue federal funding beyond the Oct. 1 start of the new 1998 fiscal year.
The House and the Senate were scheduled to vote on the compromise before the end of the day.
